cases.purpose: Controlled real growth between probe and read, and eight-round ERANGE exhaustion for path, fd and nofollow system calls.
cases.oracle: The original deferral requirements, the documented builtins and independent Linux syscall/socket/fd semantics. Positive and negative controls use separate Python/ctypes callers in setup, never candidate output. The xattr writer changes a real attribute while its first data syscall is stopped; the kernel executes that read after the change and supplies the real ERANGE.
cases.comparison: A pinned seccomp supervisor is extended only in a new VM-only wrapper. It retains every notified syscall and reply; sender fdinfo is read while sendto is paused. Before/after shell and exec-child fd tables, raw datagrams, status and diagnostics are captured. For xattr the unfiltered supervisor verifies the actual old and new values before continuing the data call; the candidate must reprobe, return the exact grown bytes, and stop after exactly eight injected ERANGEs.
cases.stdout:
xattr-path growth=yes exhaustion=yes
xattr-fd growth=yes exhaustion=yes
xattr-nofollow growth=yes exhaustion=yes

cases.purpose: Flag isolation, exec inheritance and close for TCP, Unix, UDP, accept and PTY descriptors, plus closed and nonnumeric fd diagnostics.
cases.oracle: The original bashpoll deferral requirements and Linux fcntl, /proc fdinfo, exec inheritance, signal mask, epoll and signalfd interfaces. Setup independently proves descriptor and PTY flag observations or a self-sent signalfd signal with 128-byte siginfo and a preblocked mask.
cases.comparison: A private shell owns the descriptors and receives only self-generated signals; independent subprocesses read its fdinfo or SigBlk. Each flag bit, inherited child descriptor, closed descriptor and invalid diagnostic is compared; the signal case separately checks wait readability and siginfo after exec in the same PID. Unload is explicitly retained as a gap because these builds have a compiled-in builtin.
